findings.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)` matches the raw client-supplied string with no URL normalization (scheme, host case, trailing slash, query string, fragment), so `http://host/a`, `https://host/a/`, and `http://host/a?utm_source=x` each miss the lookup, and TopicRetriever#fetch_http then creates a separate duplicate topic for every variant because the only check is the host (P1, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — every lookup miss for any URL on the embeddable host runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, which downloads the whole feed and re-imports every item, and the throttle is keyed per URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so N distinct missing URLs trigger N full feed polls with no feed-level cache (the unused `feed_key` shows this cache was planned but never built) (P2, conf 100)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — the check-then-insert (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `PostCreator#create` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) races between the hourly PollFeed, the inline PollFeed run from RetrieveTopic, and unthrottled staff RetrieveTopic jobs; the loser gets RecordNotUnique from the unique index after PostCreator has already enqueued jobs for a post that is then rolled back, and the exception stops `rss.items.each` for every remaining feed item (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — topic_embeds has no FK or dependent cleanup, and Post/Topic have no association back to it, so after the post or topic is trashed `embed.post` is nil (Trashable default scope) and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises, which aborts the hourly feed import for every item after it on every run, while `topic_id_for_embed` keeps returning the trashed topic id and the embed can never be retrieved again (P1, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — the update path only writes raw through `revise!` and never updates the topic title from the new feed/readability title, so title changes at the source leave the Discourse topic title stale, while content_sha1 (line 37) marks the embed as fully in sync (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs whether or not `revise!` saved (PostRevisor#update_post ignores the `@post.save` result), and the hash covers only the source content plus the I18n footer, never the stored post, so a failed save leaves the derived hash out of step with the post forever and a moderator's local edit is silently overwritten the next time the source changes (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — content_sha1 is computed over contents after appending `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`, so changing that translation or the site locale changes the hash of every imported item and the next poll revises (new version + topic bump) every embedded topic at once (P3, conf 75)

app/models/post.rb:133 — `cook_method` is a permanent per-post switch with no rule for when it changes: PostRevisor never resets it, so any later edit of an imported post through the normal composer is saved as raw HTML and its markdown is not rendered, which also means cooking behavior now depends on a hidden column instead of on the content (P2, conf 75)

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `default: 1, null: false` hard-codes the ordinal of `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, so reordering or adding a value at the front of Post.cook_methods silently changes what every existing row and every new default row means (P3, conf 50)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, so `//cdn.example.com/img.png` becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png` (line 70 does the same for img src) and every CDN-hosted asset in imported content breaks (P2, conf 100)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — the port is dropped whenever it is 80 or 443, whatever the scheme, so `https://host:80/` and `http://host:443/` produce wrong absolute URLs; the check should compare against `uri.default_port` (P3, conf 50)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is an exact, case-sensitive comparison against one scalar host, so `www.example.com` versus `example.com`, or an embeddable_host typed in uppercase or with a port, rejects valid embeds, and lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 repeats the same fragile comparison on a different field (embed_url rather than referer) (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic without the checks that TopicRetriever applies (embed_url host, embed_by_username existing), so when those fail the loading page's 30-second `document.location.reload()` (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9) enqueues a job on every reload for as long as the iframe stays open and never finishes loading (P2, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is not atomic, so a crash between the two calls leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL and that URL is throttled permanently for non-staff; use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (P3, conf 50)

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255) and carries the unique index, but embed_url comes from arbitrary client and feed URLs; a longer URL raises in `TopicEmbed.create!` after PostCreator has already run, so long URLs can never be embedded and they abort the feed loop (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:25 — topic_embeds stores both topic_id and post_id when topic_id is derivable from post.topic_id, and the controller reads only topic_id, so moving the post to another topic (supported by Discourse) leaves the embed pointing at the old topic while updates go to the post in the new one (P3, conf 50)

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — switching the Disqus importer to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` breaks its existing contract: the `--category` option is removed, the thread's original `created_at` is no longer applied (topics are dated at import time), the topic body changes from a permalink to a scraped raw_html copy of the page, and one HTTP failure in `open(url)` aborts the whole import (P2, conf 100)

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `import_remote` now returns the existing post for threads already imported, but the reply loop that follows is not idempotent, so re-running the import appends a second copy of every Disqus comment to the existing topics (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` (and `topic_id_for_embed` at :79, `TopicRetriever` exists? at lib/topic_retriever.rb:37) matches the raw string with no normalization, so trailing-slash, http/https, www/apex, fragment and utm-query variants of the same article each create a separate topic, and a feed-imported `i.link` that differs from the page's `discourseEmbedUrl` spawns a duplicate topic via `import_remote` despite the unique index (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — the controller gates only on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` while the retrieval path it triggers also requires `embed_by_username` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 `return if user.blank?`), so with embed_by_username blank or pointing at a nonexistent user every embed renders `loading` forever, reloading every 30s (loading.html.erb:9) and enqueuing a `retrieve_topic` job per viewer per reload that never produces a topic (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is an exact case-sensitive single-host compare, so a blog served at both `www.example.com` and `example.com` (or with a differently-cased/space-padded setting value) gets InvalidAccess on one variant with no multi-host or normalization support, and the same exact compare in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 rejects those embed URLs too (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10 — the controller never validates that `embed_url`'s host matches `embeddable_host` or has an http(s) scheme before enqueuing, deferring it to TopicRetriever which silently drops it, so an off-host or non-URL embed_url renders the `loading` page with a perpetual 30s reload loop instead of an error (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, so `//cdn.example.com/a.png` is rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png`, and relative links not starting with `/` (`images/a.png`, `../a.html`) are left untouched and resolve against the Discourse host, producing broken links/images in imported posts (same at :70 for img src) (P2, conf 100)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every item has a `content` element, but plain RSS 2.0 items only carry `<description>` so `i.content` is nil and the whole poll aborts with NoMethodError, meaning the most common feed format is not supported and no remaining items are imported (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — `topic_id_for_embed` returns the topic_id even after a moderator deletes the topic/post, so `TopicView.new` at embed_controller.rb:13 raises NotFound and the embed is permanently broken with no re-import path, while the update branch at :32 revises a trashed `embed.post` (P2, conf 50)

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:24 — referer validation is only tested with no referer; there is no spec for a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, nor for an off-host embed_url, and there are no specs for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` (feed_polling_enabled on/off, blank embed_by_username), `PollFeed#poll_feed` item parsing, or `absolutize_urls` with ports/protocol-relative URLs, so the core URL-validation acceptance criteria are unverified (P2, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:40 — the `feed_polling_enabled?` branch runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously on every uncached embed request, and on a feed miss it falls through to `fetch_http` without checking `feed_polling_url`, so there is no setting that turns off arbitrary-page scraping when a site wants feed-only import (P3, conf 50)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to the `loading` render as well as the topic view, so after the topic is created, intermediaries and the browser serve the cached loading page on the 30s reload and the discussion appears up to a minute late (P3, conf 50)

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on the Postgres versions of this era (pre-11) rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking every read and write on posts for the length of the rewrite on large forums; the safe path is add nullable column, set default, backfill in batches, then add NOT NULL (P2, conf 75)

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration does nothing on existing installs, since the version is already in schema_migrations, but any re-run (db:migrate:redo, a restored schema_migrations, a down/up) now silently drops and recreates top_topics with all its rows instead of failing loudly (P3, conf 75)

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` silently drops any existing topic_embeds table and its embed_url->topic mappings when the migration re-runs, after which TopicEmbed.import and TopicRetriever find no embed and create duplicate topics for every URL they already imported (P2, conf 50)

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — `t.integer :topic_id, null: false` / `t.integer :post_id, null: false` have no foreign key and no cleanup when a topic or post is deleted, and the unique index on embed_url keeps the orphan row in place: TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the deleted topic id, TopicRetriever returns early because the embed `exists?`, and TopicEmbed.import calls `PostRevisor.new(embed.post)` with a nil post, so that URL can never be re-imported (P2, conf 75)

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url, null: false` is varchar(255) and TopicEmbed has no length validation, so any article URL over 255 chars makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise inside the import transaction; that URL is never stored and the exception aborts the rest of the PollFeed feed loop (P2, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes SimpleRSS exposes `content` for every item, but SimpleRSS 1.3.1 only sets `:content` for Atom `<content>`; RSS 2.0 items come back as `{:title, :link, :description, :content_encoded, :guid}` (checked against the installed gem), so `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError on the first item, aborting the whole poll for any RSS 2.0 feed even though the setting says "RSS/ATOM" (P1, conf 100)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — the fallback `url = i.id` never works for RSS 2.0 because SimpleRSS stores the item identifier under `:guid`, not `:id`, so RSS items without an http link get a nil url and `TopicEmbed.import` silently drops them (P3, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby 2.1+, and nothing in the Gemfile adds a backport (no scrub_rb) even though the Gemfile still targets 1.9/2.0-era runtimes ("perftools only works on 1.9 atm"), so feed polling raises NoMethodError on those rubies (P2, conf 50)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` without `require 'open-uri'` (only poll_feed.rb requires it), so when the class is loaded outside the jobs path, e.g. the rewritten `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` import, `Kernel#open` treats "http://..." as a local file path and raises Errno::ENOENT (P2, conf 50)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — The stated intent is "enhance embed URL handling and validation", but the change builds a whole new embedding feature (all target files were empty blobs e69de29): hourly RSS/Atom feed import, remote scraping via ruby-readability, and a new raw_html post render mode that skips validation. Nobody has signed off on that bigger objective (P1, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — The URL check `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses Ruby's line anchor `^`, so a multi-line value such as "javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x" passes. That URL is then placed unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` on line 13 inside a raw_html post, so the check is weaker than the "validation" the task promises (P1, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Feed content goes through `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and is stored with cook_method raw_html (topic_embed.rb:22), which returns `raw` unchanged (post.rb:133) and is shown with `raw post.cooked`. Feed HTML is never sanitized, which reverses the "validation" intent (P1, conf 75)

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` adds a general way to skip validation to the shared PostRevisor, used here with `skip_validations: true` (topic_embed.rb:36). A task about adding validation instead weakens model validation for any caller (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:55 — The comment says "Convert any relative URLs to absolute", but the code only rewrites hrefs/srcs that start with '/'. Paths like "img/a.png" or "../x" stay unchanged, and protocol-relative "//cdn.example.com/x" gets mangled into "http://host/cdn.example.com/x" (P2, conf 100)

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an equality test. Any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. "https://forum.example.co" for "https://forum.example.com/") is accepted and can resize the iframe, so the origin validation is weaker than it looks (P2, conf 75)

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — The Disqus importer was quietly changed. The `--category` option is gone, the topic `created_at` is no longer kept, and the permalink post is replaced by live-fetching and scraping each thread URL through TopicEmbed.import_remote. None of this is part of the embed URL validation intent (P2, conf 100)

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — An unrelated, already-shipped migration was edited to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops an existing table on re-run. This is outside the task's intent and has no stated acceptance (P2, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:25 — The comment "Throttle other users to once every 60 seconds" is wrong: the Redis key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so the throttle is global per URL, not per user, and one visitor's request blocks retrieval for everyone for 60s (P3, conf 75)

app/models/post.rb:131 — The comment says raw HTML is for "posts imported via RSS", but TopicEmbed.import_remote (HTTP scraping, used by TopicRetriever and the Disqus importer) also creates raw_html posts, so the comment understates where unsanitized rendering applies (P3, conf 75)

config/locales/server.en.yml:768 — The embeddable_host description "Host that can embed the comments" leaves out that the same setting also restricts which URLs the server will fetch and import (topic_retriever.rb invalid_host?), and that matching is exact (no www/subdomain/port), so admins get a misleading description (P3, conf 75)

config/locales/server.en.yml:769 — The feed_polling_enabled description "import a RSS/ATOM feed as posts" is inaccurate: each feed item creates a new topic (PostCreator with title) and existing ones are revised in place (P3, conf 50)

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — The test is named "is 404 without an embed_url", but ensure_embeddable runs first and raises InvalidAccess (403) because embeddable_host is not set, and the test only checks `should_not be_success`. The missing-embed_url path is never actually tested (P3, conf 75)

config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — The locale string `embed.permalink: "Permalink"` is added but nothing uses it; the only permalink behavior (the Disqus import raw) was removed in this same change (P3, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` fetches the remote page with no open/read timeout, no size cap, and no rescue, so a slow or huge embedding-site response pins a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and any OpenURI::HTTPError/SocketError/Timeout::Error escapes TopicRetriever and crashes Jobs::RetrieveTopic (P1, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no timeout, size cap, or rescue, so a hung feed host blocks the worker with `retry: false`, and because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41) calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously, any feed fetch/parse error (HTTPError, SimpleRSSError) aborts RetrieveTopic before `fetch_http` runs, so a broken feed blocks every on-demand embed retrieval (P1, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` has no per-item rescue, so one poison item (nil `i.content` on RSS items that only have <description> raising NoMethodError on `.scrub`, an unparseable link raising URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, a RecordNotUnique race) aborts the whole loop, and since feed order is stable the same item fails first every hour, silently blocking all subsequent items forever (P1, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` commits the 60s throttle key before retrieval runs, so when perform_retrieve raises, the Sidekiq retry (first backoff ~15-45s in sidekiq 2.15) hits `retrieved_recently?` == true and completes as a silent no-op success, consuming the retry without doing any work (P2, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:28 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is non-atomic, so a process kill/Redis error between the two calls leaves a TTL-less `retrieved:<url>` key and that URL is permanently throttled for all non-staff viewers (P2, conf 50)

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000)` reloads with no attempt bound or give-up state, so when retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username blank/missing user at lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 returning silently, host mismatch, persistent fetch failure) every open embed iframe spins on "Loading Discussion..." forever and enqueues a new retrieve_topic job every 30s per viewer (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — `if post.present?` treats PostCreator#create's return value as success, but PostCreator returns the unsaved @post after an ActiveRecord::Rollback (e.g. rollback_if_host_spam_detected, which is swallowed inside the enclosing `Topic.transaction` without rolling back), so `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, ..., post_id: post.id)` runs with nil post_id and raises a NOT NULL StatementInvalid instead of returning a clean failure (P2, conf 50)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — TopicEmbed.import does check-then-insert (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then create) with no RecordNotUnique handling, and the hourly PollFeed runs concurrently with PollFeed invocations triggered by each RetrieveTopic job (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41), so two workers importing the same feed item both create topics and the loser raises RecordNotUnique, crashing its job and aborting its feed loop (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `post = embed.post` returns nil once the imported post is trashed (Post includes Trashable's default scope), so the next changed-content import calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` and raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw`, which crashes PollFeed every hour for that item (P2, conf 50)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally after `revisor.revise!` without checking its return value, so a revise that returns false (post save halted) still records the new hash and the change is never retried on later polls (P3, conf 50)

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — `post.user.small_avatar_url` has no nil guard, so one post whose user has been deleted raises NoMethodError and turns the whole embed iframe into a raw 500 (P3, conf 50)

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — The diff edits an already-shipped migration unrelated to embedding (`create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`): databases that already ran it never pick up the change, fresh or re-run setups silently DROP an existing top_topics table, and nothing in the embed URL task justifies touching TopTopic schema history (P1, conf 100)

db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:3 — The diff edits an already-shipped, unrelated word-count migration with whitespace-only noise (trailing spaces stripped on line 3, trailing newline removed at EOF), which churns migration history and blame for zero functional value traceable to the embed task (P3, conf 100)

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Swapping the Disqus importer to `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` removes the `--category` option and drops `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so every Disqus import now fetches each remote link over HTTP, lands in no category, and is stamped with the current time instead of the original thread date; this regression of an unrelated import tool is not required by "embed URL handling and validation" (P1, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:11 — An hourly scheduled RSS/Atom feed importer (`recurrence { hourly }` + `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) plus three new site settings (feed_polling_enabled, feed_polling_url, embed_by_username) is a new content-ingestion feature, not URL handling/validation, and is untraceable to the stated task (P2, conf 75)

app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` changes core Post cooking for the whole forum and bypasses the entire cook/sanitize pipeline and `after_post_cook` plugin filters, backed by a new `posts.cook_method` column migration; a site-wide core-model behavior change of this breadth exceeds an embed URL validation task (P1, conf 75)

Gemfile:210 — Two new runtime gems (`gem 'ruby-readability', require: false` and `gem 'simple-rss', require: false`, plus transitive guess_html_encoding) are added for feed importing and article scraping, expanding the dependency surface beyond URL handling/validation, and only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated (P2, conf 75)

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` adds a validation-bypass option to the shared core PostRevisor used by all post edits, which is the opposite of the task's stated "validation" intent, and the same hunk deletes an unrelated blank line at line 14 (P2, conf 75)

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — The task spec body is only "Review the change.", so none of the ~650 added lines (feed polling, raw-HTML cooking, Disqus importer rewrite, new gems, migration edits) is traceable to a stated requirement, and the title "Enhance embed URL handling and validation system" misdescribes a diff that introduces a brand-new embedding feature rather than enhancing an existing one (P2, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `"#{url}"` interpolates the attacker-supplied embed_url unescaped into a raw_html post, and a URL like `http:///?'onmouseover='alert(1)'` passes both `URI(@embed_url).host` (verified on Ruby 2.6) and `/^https?\:\/\//`, so an anonymous curl request to /embed/best with a forged Referer header creates stored XSS that runs on the forum origin (P1, conf 75)

app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` skips the sanitizing cook pipeline, so remote HTML imported by TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability keeps `a[href]`/`img[src]` including `javascript:` URIs) is rendered verbatim via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19) and in the normal topic view, which gives stored XSS on the forum origin to anyone who can put content on the embeddable host page, e.g. blog comments (P1, conf 75)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` entity-decodes RSS item bodies and TopicEmbed.import stores them as raw_html with no sanitization, so any `<script>` or event-handler markup in a feed item (including third-party content syndicated into the feed) executes on the forum origin for every reader (P2, conf 75)

lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — the throttle key `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` covers only the exact URL string, and the only gate before it is a Referer header that non-browser clients set freely (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26), so an unauthenticated attacker who changes the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) enqueues unlimited jobs; each job re-runs the full RSS poll synchronously (topic_retriever.rb:41), fetches the embeddable host, and creates a new topic with `skip_validations: true`, turning the forum into a request amplifier and a topic-spam/DB flood vector (P1, conf 75)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` goes through open-uri, which follows redirects with no IP, port or scheme allow-list, no timeout and no size cap, and invalid_host? checks only the hostname, so `http://<embeddable_host>:6379/` or an open redirect on the embeddable host reaching 169.254.169.254 or internal services makes the server fetch internal resources and publish the response body as a public topic (full-read SSRF), and a slow or huge response ties up Sidekiq workers (P1, conf 50)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)` matches the raw client-supplied string with no URL normalization (scheme, host case, trailing slash, query string, fragment), so `http://host/a`, `https://host/a/`, and `http://host/a?utm_source=x` each miss the lookup, and TopicRetriever#fetch_http then creates a separate duplicate topic for every variant because the only check is the host (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` doing an exact-string lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`) with no normalization, and `TopicRetriever` only validates the host (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`) before calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, which persists `embed_url` as-is and enforces uniqueness only on the raw string via a unique index. Therefore different but equivalent URL variants (scheme, trailing slash, query params, fragments, host case) will miss the lookup/exists? checks and can create separate topics/embeds for the same underlying page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — every lookup miss for any URL on the embeddable host runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, which downloads the whole feed and re-imports every item, and the throttle is keyed per URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so N distinct missing URLs trigger N full feed polls with no feed-level cache (the unused `feed_key` shows this cache was planned but never built) (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the embed isn’t found yet, before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` unconditionally downloads/parses the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates all items on each call, with no feed-level throttling/caching. Meanwhile `retrieved_recently?` throttles by per-URL key (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct missing URLs on the same embeddable host can indeed trigger many full feed polls. `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key` exists but is unused, supporting the “planned cache not implemented” point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — the check-then-insert (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `PostCreator#create` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) races between the hourly PollFeed, the inline PollFeed run from RetrieveTopic, and unthrottled staff RetrieveTopic jobs; the loser gets RecordNotUnique from the unique index after PostCreator has already enqueued jobs for a post that is then rolled back, and the exception stops `rss.items.each` for every remaining feed item (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then, if blank, `TopicEmbed.create!`). Because the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, concurrent callers (e.g., scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` vs `TopicRetriever` triggering `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`, plus multiple `RetrieveTopic` jobs) can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue around `TopicEmbed.import`, and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without exception handling, so one such exception would abort processing of the remaining feed items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — topic_embeds has no FK or dependent cleanup, and Post/Topic have no association back to it, so after the post or topic is trashed `embed.post` is nil (Trashable default scope) and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises, which aborts the hourly feed import for every item after it on every run, while `topic_id_for_embed` keeps returning the trashed topic id and the embed can never be retrieved again (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` when the content hash changes, with no guard for `post` being nil (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the else/update block). Since the migration adds `topic_embeds.topic_id`/`post_id` without any FK constraints or dependent cleanup, it’s possible for a `TopicEmbed` row to outlive its `post`/`topic` (or have the association not resolve), making `embed.post` nil and causing an exception during feed polling. Separately, `TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve` returns early if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so an orphaned/stale `TopicEmbed` row will permanently block re-retrieval for that URL, and `topic_id_for_embed` will keep returning the stored topic_id regardless of whether the topic still exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — the update path only writes raw through `revise!` and never updates the topic title from the new feed/readability title, so title changes at the source leave the Discourse topic title stale, while content_sha1 (line 37) marks the embed as fully in sync (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch (when `embed` exists) only revises the post raw via `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` and then updates `embed.content_sha1` (computed solely from `contents`). There is no code path that updates the topic title on updates, and because `content_sha1` ignores `title`, a source title change alone will not trigger any update and will leave the Discourse topic title stale while the embed is treated as up-to-date (`content_sha1` unchanged).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs whether or not `revise!` saved (PostRevisor#update_post ignores the `@post.save` result), and the hash covers only the source content plus the I18n footer, never the stored post, so a failed save leaves the derived hash out of step with the post forever and a moderator's local edit is silently overwritten the next time the source changes (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, `revisor.revise!(...)` is called and then `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally (app/models/topic_embed.rb). In PostRevisor#update_post, the diff changes the save to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` but still does not check the return value or raise on failure, so a failed save (e.g., DB-level constraint) would not prevent `content_sha1` from being updated, leaving the embed hash out of sync with the actual stored post.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — content_sha1 is computed over contents after appending `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`, so changing that translation or the site locale changes the hash of every imported item and the next poll revises (new version + topic bump) every embedded topic at once (P3, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents` is mutated by appending a localized `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)` footer before computing `content_sha1` (`contents << ...` then `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`). That makes the stored SHA depend on the current translation/locale, so changing translations (or running under a different locale) will change the hash even if the upstream feed content is identical, causing `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and triggering `PostRevisor` updates for all previously imported items on the next poll.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `cook_method` is a permanent per-post switch with no rule for when it changes: PostRevisor never resets it, so any later edit of an imported post through the normal composer is saved as raw HTML and its markdown is not rendered, which also means cooking behavior now depends on a hidden column instead of on the content (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a persistent per-post `cook_method` flag (Post.cook_methods + `posts.cook_method` column) and changes `Post#cook` to bypass cooking when `cook_method == :raw_html` by returning `raw` directly. Imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (TopicEmbed.import -> PostCreator). There is no corresponding logic in the diff to ever change/reset `cook_method` on later revisions (PostRevisor changes shown do not touch it), so an imported post will continue to bypass the markdown/cooking pipeline even after normal edits. Whether that's a defect is not provable from the diff (it may be intended for imported HTML), but it is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/architecture concern: rendering depends on a hidden column with no transition rule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `default: 1, null: false` hard-codes the ordinal of `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, so reordering or adding a value at the front of Post.cook_methods silently changes what every existing row and every new default row means (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. The `default: 1` does implicitly depend on the enum’s ordering/ordinal for what “1” means, so future reordering or prepending new enum values could change the meaning of existing rows. However, the diff does not show any actual misbehavior right now (and Discourse-style enums are typically 1-based, so `1` likely maps to `:regular`), making this a maintainability/robustness concern rather than a verifiable defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, so `//cdn.example.com/img.png` becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png` (line 70 does the same for img src) and every CDN-hosted asset in imported content breaks (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both the link and image rewriting logic check `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')`. That condition is also true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The subsequent rewrite `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` strips both leading slashes and incorrectly turns it into `http(s)://<original-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking CDN/protocol-relative assets. Same issue exists for `img` `src` rewriting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — the port is dropped whenever it is 80 or 443, whatever the scheme, so `https://host:80/` and `http://host:443/` produce wrong absolute URLs; the check should compare against `uri.default_port` (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix is built as `scheme://host` and the port is only appended when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This unconditionally treats 80 and 443 as “default” regardless of scheme. For URLs like `https://host:80/...` or `http://host:443/...`, the method will incorrectly drop the explicit non-default port, producing wrong absolute URLs. The finding’s suggestion to compare against the scheme’s default (e.g., `uri.default_port`) is consistent with the defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is an exact, case-sensitive comparison against one scalar host, so `www.example.com` versus `example.com`, or an embeddable_host typed in uppercase or with a port, rejects valid embeds, and lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 repeats the same fragile comparison on a different field (embed_url rather than referer) (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce exact string host comparisons in two places: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable checks `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and TopicRetriever#invalid_host? checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/UX/design concern because a single scalar `embeddable_host` setting plus exact matching will reject requests when the embed page uses a different but related hostname (e.g., `www.` vs apex) or if an admin enters the setting in an unexpected format. However, strict matching may also be intentional as a security control (only one allowed host), so it’s not clearly a “defect” purely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic without the checks that TopicRetriever applies (embed_url host, embed_by_username existing), so when those fail the loading page's 30-second `document.location.reload()` (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9) enqueues a job on every reload for as long as the iframe stays open and never finishes loading (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no existing TopicEmbed is found it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15-18). The loading template then forces a reload every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-11). The enqueued job runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can bail out forever without creating an embed if preconditions fail (e.g., `invalid_host?` when `URI(@embed_url).host` != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, or `fetch_http` returning if `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` user is missing). Those checks are not performed before enqueuing, so the iframe can repeatedly enqueue jobs on every reload while never transitioning out of the loading state, causing job spam/backlog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is not atomic, so a crash between the two calls leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL and that URL is throttled permanently for non-staff; use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two commands are not atomic; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can be left without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever and the URL to be treated as “retrieved recently” permanently for non-staff. The diff clearly shows this pattern and the resulting permanent throttle behavior is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255) and carries the unique index, but embed_url comes from arbitrary client and feed URLs; a longer URL raises in `TopicEmbed.create!` after PostCreator has already run, so long URLs can never be embedded and they abort the feed loop (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the column `t.string :embed_url` uses the default string limit (typically 255) and is uniquely indexed. `TopicEmbed.import` passes arbitrary feed/client URLs directly into `TopicEmbed.create!` without length validation or rescue. If a URL exceeds the column limit, the DB insert will raise and (since `poll_feed` iterates items without handling exceptions) the job/feed loop can abort. Although the PostCreator call occurs earlier, it is inside a `Topic.transaction`, so the post/topic would roll back—but the long URL still cannot be stored/embedded and the exception can stop processing further items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:25 — topic_embeds stores both topic_id and post_id when topic_id is derivable from post.topic_id, and the controller reads only topic_id, so moving the post to another topic (supported by Discourse) leaves the embed pointing at the old topic while updates go to the post in the new one (P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces redundant storage of both `topic_id` and `post_id` on `topic_embeds` (migration + `TopicEmbed.create!`). Later, lookup for display uses only the stored `topic_id` (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` plucks `:topic_id`, and `EmbedController#best` builds `TopicView` from that). Updates, however, operate via `embed.post` (`TopicEmbed#import` loads `post = embed.post` and revises that post) and never reconcile `topic_embeds.topic_id` with `post.topic_id` (only `content_sha1` is updated). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` has no per-item rescue, so one poison item (nil `i.content` on RSS items that only have <description> raising NoMethodError on `.scrub`, an unparseable link raising URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, a RecordNotUnique race) aborts the whole loop, and since feed order is stable the same item fails first every hour, silently blocking all subsequent items forever (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item error handling. If any item has `i.content == nil` (common when a feed only provides `<description>`), `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the entire job. Likewise, `TopicEmbed.import` can raise (it calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction, which can throw on uniqueness races; and `absolutize_urls` does `URI(url)` which can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` even for strings matching the `^https?://` regex). Any such exception would prevent processing subsequent items in the same run, and since the job is scheduled hourly, a consistently-bad early item can repeatedly prevent later items from importing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` commits the 60s throttle key before retrieval runs, so when perform_retrieve raises, the Sidekiq retry (first backoff ~15-45s in sidekiq 2.15) hits `retrieved_recently?` == true and completes as a silent no-op success, consuming the retry without doing any work (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key via `setnx` and `expire` before `perform_retrieve` is called (`retrieve` does `perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)`). Since `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` can raise (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` without rescue), a failing attempt will still leave the key set for 60s. A subsequent Sidekiq retry of `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` will call `retrieve`, hit `retrieved_recently? == true`, skip work, and return successfully—consuming the retry without performing retrieval. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:28 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is non-atomic, so a process kill/Redis error between the two calls leaves a TTL-less `retrieved:<url>` key and that URL is permanently throttled for all non-staff viewers (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently? the throttle is implemented as two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is non-atomic; if the process dies or Redis errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire`, the key can be left without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely for that `retrieved:<url>` key for all requests where `@opts[:no_throttle]` is not set (i.e., non-staff). This risk is directly verifiable from the diff since this file/logic is newly added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000)` reloads with no attempt bound or give-up state, so when retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username blank/missing user at lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 returning silently, host mismatch, persistent fetch failure) every open embed iframe spins on "Loading Discussion..." forever and enqueues a new retrieve_topic job every 30s per viewer (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) reloads the iframe every 30s via `setTimeout(... document.location.reload() ...)`, which will hit `#best` again and enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job again. If retrieval can never succeed (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` is blank or user missing, or `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` rejects the `embed_url` host), the iframe will loop forever and keep enqueueing jobs (even if `retrieved_recently?` throttles actual fetching, the jobs are still created/processed repeatedly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — TopicEmbed.import does check-then-insert (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then create) with no RecordNotUnique handling, and the hourly PollFeed runs concurrently with PollFeed invocations triggered by each RetrieveTopic job (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41), so two workers importing the same feed item both create topics and the loser raises RecordNotUnique, crashing its job and aborting its feed loop (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-insert (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) while a unique index exists on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` skips the sanitizing cook pipeline, so remote HTML imported by TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability keeps `a[href]`/`img[src]` including `javascript:` URIs) is rendered verbatim via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19) and in the normal topic view, which gives stored XSS on the forum origin to anyone who can put content on the embeddable host page, e.g. blog comments (P1, conf 75)

The embed view then renders this HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Nothing in the diff strips dangerous attributes/schemes (e.g., `javascript:`), so arbitrary stored HTML from the embeddable host/feed can be rendered on the Discourse origin, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` entity-decodes RSS item bodies and TopicEmbed.import stores them as raw_html with no sanitization, so any `<script>` or event-handler markup in a feed item (including third-party content syndicated into the feed) executes on the forum origin for every reader (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: PollFeed builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the first post via `PostCreator.new(... raw: ..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skip_validations: true)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Post#cook explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (app/models/post.rb), so no sanitization is applied. The embed view also renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Therefore any `<script>` or unsafe HTML/event attributes present in feed content can be stored and rendered directly, creating an XSS vulnerability on the forum origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — the throttle key `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` covers only the exact URL string, and the only gate before it is a Referer header that non-browser clients set freely (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26), so an unauthenticated attacker who changes the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) enqueues unlimited jobs; each job re-runs the full RSS poll synchronously (topic_retriever.rb:41), fetches the embeddable host, and creates a new topic with `skip_validations: true`, turning the forum into a request amplifier and a topic-spam/DB flood vector (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an unauthenticated `/embed/best` endpoint (config/routes.rb, app/controllers/embed_controller.rb) that enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is missing. The only access check in `ensure_embeddable` is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and the throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` keys on the full `@embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying query strings on the same host will bypass throttling and enqueue many jobs. Each job can synchronously run `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (lib/topic_retriever.rb) and/or fetch remote content (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url)`), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts/topics with `skip_validations: true` and a unique index only on `embed_url`, enabling DB/topic spam via distinct URLs. This is a real, diff-grounded DoS/amplification/spam vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` goes through open-uri, which follows redirects with no IP, port or scheme allow-list, no timeout and no size cap, and invalid_host? checks only the hostname, so `http://<embeddable_host>:6379/` or an open redirect on the embeddable host reaching 169.254.169.254 or internal services makes the server fetch internal resources and publish the response body as a public topic (full-read SSRF), and a slow or huge response ties up Sidekiq workers (P1, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds remote fetching of arbitrary URLs via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` using `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and feed polling using `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), allowing nonstandard ports (e.g. `http://<host>:6379/`) and not constraining scheme. The new code also does not set timeouts, response size limits, or restrict redirect targets, so if open-uri is in effect it can be used for SSRF and worker exhaustion, and the fetched content is then published as a topic via `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: :raw_html`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` passes the Disqus export's thread link into `Kernel#open` with no URI/scheme validation (the `^https?` check in import runs only after the fetch), so a thread link starting with `|` runs a shell command on the admin's machine and a `file`-style local path reads local files into a public topic (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the diff replaces creating a topic with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (new in this diff), it calls `open(url).read` directly before any URL validation. The only `^https?` check is in `TopicEmbed.import`, which runs *after* the fetch. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — the raw_html cook_method stays on the post after import, so any later edit of an imported post through the normal PostRevisor path (by the embed_by_username account or any user allowed to edit it) is saved as raw HTML with no sanitization, which gives that editor arbitrary script execution on the forum origin (P2, conf 50)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, so any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. `https://forum.example` for `https://forum.example.com/`) passes and its messages are accepted to resize the host page's iframe (UI redress only) (P3, conf 75)

The diff clearly introduces this insecure origin validation logic in the newly added embed script.
